Dry-air regenerative carbon concentration: coupled water, ionic transport and active-area contracts
ROOT, 12 November 2026 Brisbane. These are independently derived conditional engineering screens, not an achieved separator, measured material, prototype or plant. The accompanying standard-library Python calculation and JSON evaluate the displayed formulas. No producer ZIP, code component or new physical experiment was collected or run.

1. Full useful output and current limits
The useful operation remains atmospheric air at 425 ppm CO2, oxygen present, 20--30 C and 20--40% RH to >=95% dry CO2 at 1 bar, >=50% admitted-stream removal, >=1 kg/day over 100 h, <=0.50 kWh purchased energy/kg and <=2 kg charged water/kg including preparation and startup. A 1-t/day cost calculation must pay complete equipment, preparation, replacement and operation; $100/t is a target, not a result.
The available worked amine candidate is a conditional model: its favorable industrial-hardware sensitivity is still about1.46 kWh/kg and its stated production scenario about$712/t. The commercial laboratory-component case is6.53--8.43 kWh/kg. Its 235m2 moisture-recovery screen is a different architecture, not an installed exchanger. These findings do not exclude all separators. Main-answer capture has a native prefix and labelled rendered remainder; uncollected linked code is not ROOT-executed evidence.

2. The outer gas/water barrier is not the inner ionic separator
A gas-permeable covering of a wet capture interface sees only tens of pascals of atmospheric CO2 driving pressure, but thousands of pascals of water-vapor driving pressure. A separate carbon-pump membrane can see nearly one bar of CO2 backpressure. These different functions cannot be assigned the same favorable permeability without a real architecture.
For constant permeances, a perfectly reactive CO2 sink and dilute plug flow, J_CO2=Kc*p_CO2 and J_water=Kw*Delta_pw. Integrating 50% capture gives a log-mean CO2 pressure p_lm=P*x/2/log(2). Thus m_water/m_CO2=(Mw/Mc)*(Kw/Kc)*Delta_pw/p_lm.
This is a favorable, isothermal screen: finite reactive-interface CO2, gas films, support resistance, humidity changes, defects and nonlinear sorption are omitted. It is not an all-architecture water bound.
